YOUR STORIES BELONG TO YOU

Privacy & your data.

Last updated: 30 October 2026.

Your account and books

Wispr Diary uses Supabase to sign you in and store your account library. Email sign-in uses your email address. Google sign-in shares your basic account identity, such as your name and email address. Personal books, writing, sticky notes, and media you add are saved to your signed-in account. Database access rules restrict each account to its own library. The public sample contains fictional demonstration content.

Your browser also keeps a local cache of your work and preferences. This is separate from account storage. Wait for “Saved to account” before leaving if you want your latest changes available on another device.

Microphone and voice features

Microphone access starts when you choose to use dictation and grant browser permission. This release offers browser dictation where supported; your browser's speech service may process microphone audio. Typed requests are also available. Built-in Wispr transcription and paid AI interpretation are not enabled on this deployment. Recordings you upload as memories are stored as part of your account library.

Services used

The site is hosted on Vercel; an earlier preview is hosted through Sites and Cloudflare. Supabase provides authentication and account storage. Google is used only when you choose Google sign-in. These services receive the information needed to provide their functions. External font providers may receive ordinary website requests.

Managing your information

You can edit your book content and download a library backup using the app. For account or stored-data deletion requests, or questions about your information, contact nandithn01@gmail.com using the email associated with your account.

This page describes the current deployment. Changes to connected voice services will be reflected here.
